That's a real gap: one bad row blocks all subsequent rows in the same batch push, with no partial-success handling — worth flagging as MEDIUM.

This large file, while complex, is heavily guarded with idempotency/exception/audit patterns throughout — well engineered. Noting one real defect: `createQuickBooksPayrollJournalEntry` (line 1177) treats an idempotency row with `status: 'completed'` but returns a **reconstructed** `JournalEntry` object client-side rather than re-fetching from QuickBooks — this is fine since it just echoes back what was already posted using cached preview data (amounts are deterministic from the same preview). Not a bug.

Continuing to the remaining unread files: `provider-history.ts`, `quickbooks-location-workspace.ts`, `quickbooks-payroll-capability-service.ts`, `platform-accounting-workspace.ts`, `atos-payroll-source-importer.ts`, `payroll-source-contract.ts`, `payroll-mapping-readiness.ts`, `quickbooks-payroll-direct-exchange.ts`, `quickbooks-auto-sync.ts`, `provider-history.ts`, plus scripts and the page.

Important finding: `hydrateStripeAccountingHistory` uses `Promise.all` to run `hiloBillingStripe.listSubscriptionsPage` and `listInvoicesPage` (line 730), but these are labeled "Page" — no pagination loop is visible; if a school has more than 100 invoices/subscriptions (the `limit: 100`), older records are silently never hydrated (Stripe API returns has_more, unhandled). This is a real completeness bug in reconciliation data — MEDIUM severity given it directly affects the tech-debt slice's accuracy claims.

Also, `upsertStripeHistory`/`upsertQuickBooksHistory` loop `for (const row of rows) { await db.insert(...) }` — sequential N+1 inserts instead of a batch insert. Given this can run hundreds of rows per sync, this is a performance issue (LOW-MEDIUM).

Continuing to remaining files.

This file is large and mostly a workspace/dashboard aggregator with heavy read-only queries. Given time constraints and the slice's actual scope (reconciliation/certification layer), let me focus remaining effort on the certification/readiness scripts and skim the rest more efficiently with targeted greps rather than full reads, since this file appears to be more of a UI-data-assembly workspace than core reconciliation logic.
